makarSankranti.about: Makar Sankranti marks the Sun's entry into Capricorn (Makara) and the start of Uttarayana, the Sun's northward journey. It is one of the few festivals set by the Sun rather than the Moon, so it falls on about 14–15 January every year. It is a harvest festival celebrated as Pongal, Lohri, Uttarayan and Bihu across India.
makarSankranti.story: The Mahabharata tells that Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, waited for Uttarayana to begin before leaving his body, because this half of the year is considered the most auspicious. On this day the Sun is also said to visit his son Shani, the lord of Capricorn, so it celebrates reconciliation within families.
benefits: A holy dip and charity today are said to bring many times the usual merit
Sun worship is traditionally linked with health, confidence and success
Til (sesame) and jaggery shared today bring warmth and sweetness to relationships
Marks a fresh, auspicious start for new work after the inauspicious month of Kharmas
dos: Bathe early, in a holy river if possible, or add a little Ganga jal and sesame to your bath water
Offer arghya (water) to the rising Sun
Donate til, jaggery, khichdi, blankets or warm clothes
Eat and share til-gud sweets and khichdi
donts: Don't quarrel or speak harshly on this day
Avoid alcohol and non-vegetarian food
Don't cut trees or harm animals; many people fly kites only with safe strings
makarSankranti.fasting: No strict fast. Many people eat only sattvic food, and khichdi made with new rice and urad dal is traditional.
samagri: Water, red flowers and red sandalwood
steps: Wake before sunrise and bathe, adding a few sesame seeds and Ganga jal to the water
Fill a copper lota with water, red flowers, roli, akshat and a few sesame seeds
Face east and offer the water slowly to the rising Sun, chanting Om Ghrini Suryaya Namah
Light a ghee lamp and incense before a picture of Surya Dev
Offer til-gud and khichdi as bhog and sing the aarti
Donate til, jaggery, khichdi or warm clothes to someone in need
Share til-gud with family and friends
mantraMeanings: Salutations to the radiant Sun.
Salutations to Aditya, the son of Aditi.

vasantPanchami.about: Vasant Panchami, on the fifth day of the bright half of Magha, welcomes spring and honours Goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, music and the arts. Yellow, the colour of mustard fields in bloom, is worn and offered throughout the day.
vasantPanchami.story: It is said that after creating the world, Brahma felt it was silent and lifeless. From his kamandalu he sprinkled water and Goddess Saraswati appeared with a veena; when she played, all beings found speech and the world was filled with sound. Vasant Panchami celebrates her appearance.
benefits: Blesses students with wisdom, memory and focus
Traditionally the best day to begin learning, writing or music (vidyarambh)
Considered an abujh muhurat, auspicious for new beginnings without checking further
Brings creativity and clarity of speech
dos: Wear yellow or white clothes
Place books, pens and musical instruments before the goddess for her blessing
Begin a child's first lesson, or start a new course or art
Offer yellow sweets, saffron rice and yellow flowers
donts: Don't study or write with the books kept for puja until the puja is complete
Avoid meat, alcohol and quarrels
Don't disrespect books or teachers
vasantPanchami.fasting: Optional. Some devotees fast until the puja is done and then eat sattvic food.
samagri: Picture or idol of Goddess Saraswati
Kesar (saffron) rice or yellow sweets for bhog
steps: Bathe and wear clean yellow or white clothes
Place the goddess on a yellow cloth facing east or north
Keep books, pens and instruments beside her
Offer haldi, kumkum, akshat, yellow flowers and chandan
Light the lamp and incense and chant Om Aim Saraswatyai Namah 108 times
Offer kesar rice or yellow sweets as bhog
Recite the Saraswati Vandana and pray for wisdom
Take blessings from teachers and elders
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Goddess Saraswati; 'Aim' is her seed sound.

mahaShivaratri.about: Maha Shivaratri, the great night of Shiva, falls on the 14th night of the dark half of Phalguna (Magha in the southern calendar). Devotees fast, stay awake through the night and worship Shiva in four prahars (watches), offering abhishek to the Shivling.
mahaShivaratri.story: Many stories mark this night: the marriage of Shiva and Parvati; Shiva appearing as an endless pillar of light (Jyotirlinga) before Brahma and Vishnu; and a hunter who, hiding in a bel tree all night, unknowingly dropped bel leaves and water on a Shivling below and was granted liberation for his unintended worship.
benefits: Said to wash away past sins and bring inner peace
Especially blessed for marriage, harmony between couples and family welfare
Night-long jagran and japa are believed to give great spiritual progress
Removes fear and obstacles through Shiva's grace
dos: Fast through the day and night as your health allows
Offer water, milk and bel leaves to the Shivling in each prahar
Chant Om Namah Shivaya through the night
Stay awake (jagran) with bhajan, japa or meditation
Break the fast the next morning after puja
donts: Don't offer tulsi, ketaki (kewda) flowers or turmeric to Shiva
Don't offer broken bel leaves or leaves with the stem knot facing up
Avoid grains, salt (if you can), onion, garlic and alcohol
Don't walk fully around the Shivling; stop at the water outlet and return
mahaShivaratri.fasting: Nirjala (no water) for those who can, otherwise phalahar: fruit, milk, sabudana, kuttu and singhara. Parana is done the next morning.
samagri: Shivling or a picture of Lord Shiva
Water and raw milk for abhishek
Bel (bilva) leaves, ideally with three leaflets
Dhatura, aak flowers and white flowers
Akshat (whole rice), honey, curd, ghee and sugar
steps: Bathe and take the sankalp to keep the fast and the night vigil
Clean the puja place and place the Shivling or Shiva's picture on a white cloth
First prahar: bathe the Shivling with water, then milk, chanting Om Namah Shivaya
Offer chandan, bel leaves, dhatura, flowers and akshat
Light the ghee lamp and incense and offer fruit and sweets
Repeat the abhishek in each of the four prahars: milk, curd, ghee and honey are traditional for the four
Chant Om Namah Shivaya or the Mahamrityunjaya mantra with a rudraksha mala
Sing the Shiv aarti at the end of each prahar
Next morning bathe, do a short puja, give charity and break the fast
mantraMeanings: I bow to Shiva, the auspicious one.
We worship the three-eyed Lord who nourishes all; may he free us from death as a ripe cucumber falls from its vine, and grant immortality.

holi.about: Holi is celebrated over two days at the end of Phalguna: Holika Dahan, a bonfire on the full-moon evening, and Rangwali Holi, the festival of colours, the next morning. It marks the victory of devotion over arrogance and the arrival of spring.
holi.story: The demon king Hiranyakashipu wanted everyone to worship him, but his son Prahlad remained devoted to Lord Vishnu. His sister Holika, who had a boon that fire could not burn her, sat in a fire holding Prahlad. By Vishnu's grace Holika burned and Prahlad came out unharmed. Later Vishnu appeared as Narasimha to end Hiranyakashipu.
benefits: Burns away negativity, illness and ill will symbolically in the Holika fire
Strengthens faith, as shown by Prahlad's devotion
Brings families and communities together and renews friendships
Welcomes the harvest and the energy of spring
dos: Do Holika puja at the bonfire in the evening during pradosh, avoiding Bhadra
Go around the fire three or seven times while tying raw cotton thread
Offer new wheat ears, coconut, jaggery and turmeric into the fire
Play with natural, skin-safe colours the next day
Forgive old quarrels and greet people with gulal
donts: Don't light the Holika during Bhadra kaal
Avoid chemical colours and forcing colour on unwilling people
Don't drink or drive carelessly; keep children away from the fire
Newly married brides traditionally don't watch their in-laws' first Holika
holi.fasting: No fast is required. Some people keep a light fast until Holika puja and then eat festive sattvic food.
samagri: Ears of new wheat or barley
steps: In the evening, bathe and go to the Holika pyre with your puja thali
Face east or north and sprinkle water around the pyre
Offer roli, akshat, flowers, turmeric, moong, jaggery and coconut
Wrap raw cotton thread around the pyre while walking around it three or seven times
Pray to Lord Narasimha and recite the Holika puja mantra
Once the fire is lit, offer new wheat or barley ears and roast them in it
Bring the roasted grain home as prasad and apply a little ash (vibhuti) to the forehead
Play Holi with colours the next morning
mantraMeanings: O Holika, created by the frightened to protect them; we worship you, be a source of wellbeing for us.
Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu).

ugadi.about: Ugadi (in Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana) and Gudi Padwa (in Maharashtra) mark the Hindu lunar new year on the first day of the bright half of Chaitra. Homes are cleaned, decorated with mango leaves and rangoli, and the new year's almanac (panchang) is heard.
ugadi.story: It is said that Brahma began creating the universe on this day. In Maharashtra the gudi, a raised pole with cloth and a pot, celebrates Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya and the victory of good. The bitter-sweet Ugadi pachadi reminds us that the year will bring every taste of life.
benefits: An auspicious start for the whole year
Considered good for buying a home, vehicle or gold and starting ventures
Neem and jaggery are traditionally linked with good health in the new season
Hearing the panchang shravanam brings awareness of the year ahead
dos: Take an oil bath early in the morning
Decorate the door with a mango-leaf toran and rangoli
Raise the gudi (Maharashtra) or prepare Ugadi pachadi (South)
Eat neem with jaggery for health
Listen to the reading of the new year's panchang
donts: Don't start the year with quarrels or debts
Avoid non-vegetarian food and alcohol
Don't leave the house dirty or cluttered
ugadi.fasting: No fast. A festive vegetarian meal with Ugadi pachadi or shrikhand-puri is traditional.
samagri: Mango leaves and marigold for the toran
Bamboo stick, silk cloth, copper or silver pot, neem twigs and a garland for the gudi
Neem flowers, raw mango, jaggery, tamarind, salt and chilli for pachadi
steps: Wake early, apply oil and take a head bath
Clean the house, put up the mango-leaf toran and draw rangoli
Raise the gudi at the right side of the main door, or set up the altar
Worship Brahma and Vishnu with haldi, kumkum, akshat and flowers
Offer the Ugadi pachadi or neem-jaggery as prasad
Sing the aarti and take blessings from elders
Listen to the new year's panchang and plan the year
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Brahma, the creator.
Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu).

ramNavami.about: Ram Navami celebrates the birth of Lord Rama on the ninth day of the bright half of Chaitra, at midday in Punarvasu nakshatra. It ends the nine days of Chaitra Navratri.
ramNavami.story: King Dasharatha of Ayodhya had no children. On sage Vasishtha's advice he performed the Putrakameshti yajna and received payasam to share with his queens. Kaushalya gave birth to Rama at noon, and Kaikeyi and Sumitra to Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna. Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, came to restore dharma.
benefits: Blesses the home with righteousness, harmony and family unity
Chanting Rama's name is said to remove fear and sorrow
Especially good for those wishing for children
Strengthens patience, duty and good conduct
dos: Fast until noon or through the day
Do the main puja at madhyahna, the time of Rama's birth
Read the Ramayana or Ramcharitmanas, especially the Bal Kand
Rock baby Rama in a cradle and offer panchamrit and panjiri
Feed the poor or offer food at a temple
donts: Avoid grains if you are fasting
Avoid onion, garlic, meat and alcohol
Don't speak lies or harshly; Rama is the ideal of truth
ramNavami.fasting: Many keep phalahar until noon or the whole day, eating fruit, milk and sabudana; others take one sattvic meal after the puja.
samagri: Picture or idol of Ram Darbar, or baby Rama in a cradle
steps: Bathe early and take a sankalp for the fast
Decorate the altar and place Ram Darbar or baby Rama in a cradle
At midday, bathe the idol with panchamrit and then clean water
Dress the idol, apply chandan and offer tulsi and yellow flowers
Offer panjiri, fruit and sweets as bhog
Chant Shri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram and rock the cradle
Sing the Ram stuti and aarti, then distribute prasad
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Rama.
Victory to Rama, victory to Rama.

hanumanJayanti.about: Hanuman Jayanti celebrates the birth of Lord Hanuman, the devoted servant of Rama, on the full moon of Chaitra in most of North India. (Some regions observe it in Kartika or Margashirsha.) Devotees visit temples at sunrise, read the Hanuman Chalisa and offer sindoor.
hanumanJayanti.story: Anjana and the wind god Vayu were blessed with a son of great strength. As a child, Hanuman mistook the rising Sun for a fruit and leapt to eat it. He later served Rama with complete devotion, crossing the ocean to find Sita, burning Lanka and bringing the Sanjeevani herb to save Lakshmana.
benefits: Gives courage, strength and protection from fear and negative energy
Traditionally eases the effects of Saturn and Mars
Helps with focus, discipline and self-control
Brings success in difficult tasks
dos: Visit a Hanuman temple at sunrise
Read the Hanuman Chalisa, Sundar Kand or Bajrang Baan
Offer sindoor with jasmine oil, red flowers and a red cloth
Offer boondi laddoo, gram and jaggery
Keep a pure, disciplined day
donts: Avoid meat, alcohol, onion and garlic
Women traditionally don't touch the idol or apply sindoor themselves; they pray from a little distance
Don't disrespect anyone; Hanuman is the symbol of humility
hanumanJayanti.fasting: Many fast until evening, eating fruit and milk, and break it after the evening aarti.
samagri: Red flowers and a red cloth
steps: Bathe early and wear red or orange if you can
Place Hanuman's picture on a red cloth facing south or east
Light a mustard-oil or ghee lamp and incense
Offer sindoor, red flowers, betel leaf and the red cloth
Offer laddoo, gram and jaggery as bhog
Read the Hanuman Chalisa (once, 7 or 11 times) or the Sundar Kand
Sing the Hanuman aarti and pray for strength and protection
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Hanuman; 'Ham' is his seed sound.
I take refuge in Rama's messenger, swift as the mind and the wind, master of the senses, the wisest of the wise, son of Vayu and leader of the vanaras.

akshayaTritiya.about: Akshaya Tritiya falls on the third day of the bright half of Vaishakha. 'Akshaya' means never diminishing: good deeds, charity and purchases made today are believed to grow forever. The whole day is an abujh muhurat, auspicious without checking further.
akshayaTritiya.story: Tradition holds that the Treta Yuga began on this day, that Parashurama was born, and that the Ganga descended to earth. Lord Krishna gave the Pandavas the Akshaya Patra, a vessel that never ran out of food, and Kubera received his wealth from Lakshmi. Sudama also met Krishna and found his poverty ended.
benefits: Charity and good deeds today are said to give unending merit
Auspicious for buying gold, property or vehicles and for starting ventures
Lakshmi and Vishnu worship invites lasting prosperity
Good for marriages, griha pravesh and other ceremonies
dos: Worship Lakshmi and Vishnu together
Donate water pots, fans, grain, clothes or food
Buy gold, silver or something useful for the home if you can
Start new work or investments
donts: Don't lend or borrow money today if you can avoid it
Avoid anger and harsh speech
Don't leave the home dark in the evening; light lamps
akshayaTritiya.fasting: Optional. Some fast until the puja and then eat a sattvic meal.
samagri: Lotus or red flowers and tulsi
Barley or wheat, chana dal and jaggery
Items for charity: matka (water pot), grain or clothes
steps: Bathe early and wear clean clothes
Set Lakshmi and Vishnu on the altar
Bathe the idols with panchamrit and dress them
Offer chandan, akshat, flowers and tulsi to Vishnu and lotus or red flowers to Lakshmi
Offer barley, chana dal and sweets as bhog
Chant the mantras and sing the aartis
Donate a filled water pot, grain or clothes
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Mahalakshmi; 'Shreem' is her seed sound.
Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu).

nirjalaEkadashi.about: Nirjala Ekadashi, on the 11th day of the bright half of Jyeshtha, is the strictest of the 24 Ekadashis: devotees take neither food nor water from sunrise to the next sunrise. Keeping it is said to give the merit of all the year's Ekadashis.
nirjalaEkadashi.story: Bhima, the strongest Pandava, could not bear hunger and could not keep the monthly Ekadashi fasts. Sage Vyasa told him to keep just this one Ekadashi without even water, which would give the fruit of all of them. It is therefore also called Bhimseni Ekadashi.
benefits: Said to give the merit of all 24 Ekadashis
Purifies body and mind and builds self-discipline
Brings Vishnu's grace and peace to the family
Charity of water today is considered especially meritorious
dos: Wake early, bathe and take a sankalp for the fast
Chant Vishnu's name or read the Vishnu Sahasranama
Offer tulsi leaves to Lord Vishnu
Stay awake longer in the evening for bhajan if you can
Break the fast (parana) the next morning within the Dwadashi time
Donate water, a filled water pot, fans or umbrellas
donts: Don't eat rice or grains, even if you are not fasting
Don't pluck tulsi leaves on Ekadashi; pick them the day before
Avoid onion, garlic, alcohol and meat
Avoid anger, gossip and sleeping in the day
Don't take on this fast if you are pregnant, ill or elderly; a phalahar fast is fine
nirjalaEkadashi.fasting: Nirjala: no food or water from sunrise until parana the next morning. Those who can't should keep a fruit and milk fast instead.
samagri: Picture or idol of Lord Vishnu or Krishna
Fruits, dry fruits and sweets for bhog
Matka (clay pot) filled with water for donation
steps: Wake before sunrise, bathe and take the sankalp for a nirjala fast
Clean the altar and place Lord Vishnu on a yellow cloth
Bathe the idol with panchamrit and then water
Offer chandan, yellow flowers and tulsi leaves
Light the lamp and chant Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya
Read the Ekadashi katha and sing the aarti
Donate a filled water pot or water to the thirsty
Next morning, after puja, break the fast with water and light food within the Dwadashi time
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu), the indweller of all.

devshayaniEkadashi.about: Devshayani (Ashadhi) Ekadashi, on the 11th day of the bright half of Ashadha, is when Lord Vishnu is believed to go into yoga-nidra on the serpent Shesha. It begins Chaturmas, the four holy months when weddings and other big ceremonies are usually avoided. In Maharashtra lakhs of devotees walk to Pandharpur for Lord Vitthal.
devshayaniEkadashi.story: King Mandhata's kingdom suffered a long drought. Sage Angiras told him to keep the Ashadha Shukla Ekadashi fast, and soon rain returned and the land prospered. Vishnu's rest for four months is also tied to his promise to King Bali to guard his kingdom.
benefits: Begins Chaturmas, a time for vows, discipline and spiritual practice
Removes sins and brings Vishnu's protection
Brings rain, prosperity and wellbeing, as in the story of Mandhata
Starting a good habit or vow today is especially meritorious
dos: Wake early, bathe and take a sankalp for the fast
Chant Vishnu's name or read the Vishnu Sahasranama
Offer tulsi leaves to Lord Vishnu
Stay awake longer in the evening for bhajan if you can
Break the fast (parana) the next morning within the Dwadashi time
Take a small vow for Chaturmas, such as giving up a food or reading scripture daily
donts: Don't eat rice or grains, even if you are not fasting
Don't pluck tulsi leaves on Ekadashi; pick them the day before
Avoid onion, garlic, alcohol and meat
Avoid anger, gossip and sleeping in the day
Avoid weddings, griha pravesh and similar ceremonies until Dev Uthani Ekadashi
devshayaniEkadashi.fasting: Fruit and milk (phalahar) or nirjala as your health allows. Parana next morning in the Dwadashi time.
samagri: Picture or idol of Lord Vishnu or Krishna
Fruits, dry fruits and sweets for bhog
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp for the fast
Place Lord Vishnu on a yellow cloth and bathe him with panchamrit
Offer yellow cloth, chandan, flowers and tulsi
Light the lamp and chant Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya
Read the Devshayani Ekadashi katha
At night lay the deity to rest on a small bed and sing the aarti
Break the fast the next morning in the Dwadashi time
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu), the indweller of all.

guruPurnima.about: Guru Purnima, the full moon of Ashadha, honours teachers and spiritual guides. It is also Vyasa Purnima, the birthday of Maharishi Veda Vyasa, who divided the Vedas and wrote the Mahabharata.
guruPurnima.story: Veda Vyasa, born on this full moon, arranged the Vedas into four, composed the eighteen Puranas and the Mahabharata, and gave the world the Bhagavad Gita through it. In Buddhist tradition, the Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath on this day.
benefits: Brings the guru's blessings for knowledge and right direction
Good day to begin spiritual practice or take initiation
Expresses gratitude, which brings humility and peace
Students are blessed with focus and wisdom
dos: Visit your guru or teacher and offer flowers, fruit or dakshina
Worship Vyasa and read from the Gita or a scripture
Begin or renew a spiritual practice
Thank parents and teachers, who are your first gurus
donts: Don't speak ill of teachers or elders
Avoid meat and alcohol
Don't waste the day; spend some time in study or meditation
guruPurnima.fasting: Optional. Some keep a fast until moonrise or eat only sattvic food.
samagri: Picture of Vyasa, your guru or ishta devata
Dakshina and a gift for your teacher
steps: Bathe early and wear clean clothes
Place a picture of Vyasa or your guru on a clean cloth
Offer chandan, flowers, a garland and akshat
Light the lamp and recite the Guru mantra
Offer fruit and sweets and sing the aarti
Visit or call your guru and teachers, touch their feet and offer dakshina
Spend time reading the Gita or meditating
mantraMeanings: The guru is Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara; the guru is the supreme reality itself. Salutations to that guru.

rakshaBandhan.deity: Family deities; the bond of protection
rakshaBandhan.about: Raksha Bandhan, on the full moon of Shravana, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters tie a rakhi on their brothers' wrists and pray for their wellbeing; brothers promise lifelong protection.
rakshaBandhan.story: When Krishna cut his finger, Draupadi tore her sari and tied it round the wound; Krishna later protected her honour in the Kaurava court. In another story Goddess Lakshmi tied a thread on King Bali and asked for Vishnu's return home, which gave us the rakhi mantra.
benefits: Strengthens the bond of love and protection in the family
The sacred thread is believed to guard against harm
Renews family ties and forgives old differences
Many people also renew their sacred thread (Shravani) today
dos: Tie the rakhi in the afternoon, outside Bhadra kaal
Prepare a thali with roli, akshat, rakhi, lamp and sweets
Apply tilak, tie the rakhi with the mantra and do aarti for your brother
Brothers give a gift and a promise of protection
Tie rakhi to cousins and friends you consider siblings
donts: Don't tie the rakhi during Bhadra kaal or Rahu Kaal
Avoid black thread or broken rakhis
Don't quarrel today
rakshaBandhan.fasting: Sisters often fast until the rakhi is tied, then eat with the family.
steps: Bathe and prepare the rakhi thali
First offer a rakhi to your family deity or Lord Ganesha
Seat your brother facing east and cover his head with a cloth
Apply roli tilak and akshat on his forehead
Tie the rakhi on his right wrist while reciting the mantra
Do aarti with the lamp and feed him a sweet
Your brother gives a gift and promises protection; take blessings of elders
mantraMeanings: With this thread that bound the mighty King Bali, I bind you; O protective thread, stay firm, do not slip.

janmashtami.about: Krishna Janmashtami celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna at midnight on the eighth day of the dark half of Bhadrapada, in Rohini nakshatra. Devotees fast all day, sing bhajans and celebrate his birth at midnight; Dahi Handi follows the next day.
janmashtami.story: King Kamsa of Mathura was told that the eighth son of his sister Devaki would kill him, so he imprisoned Devaki and Vasudeva. At midnight Krishna was born, the prison doors opened and the guards slept. Vasudeva carried the baby across the flooded Yamuna, sheltered by Sheshnag, to Gokul, where Yashoda and Nanda raised him.
benefits: Brings joy, love and devotion into the home
Fasting and night worship are said to remove sins
Blesses those wishing for children
Krishna's grace brings wisdom to face life's battles, as in the Gita
dos: Fast through the day and stay up for the midnight birth
Decorate a jhula (cradle) and the altar
At midnight bathe Laddu Gopal with panchamrit and dress him
Offer makhan-mishri, panjiri and 56 bhog if you can
Sing bhajans and chant Hare Krishna
donts: Don't eat grains during the fast
Avoid onion, garlic, meat and alcohol
Don't cut tulsi after sunset; pick leaves in the day
janmashtami.fasting: Nirjala or phalahar until midnight. The fast is broken after the midnight puja or the next morning, as per family custom.
samagri: Laddu Gopal idol and a small cradle (jhula)
New clothes, flute and peacock feather for Krishna
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp for the fast
Decorate the altar and cradle with flowers and lights
In the evening, sing bhajans and read stories of Krishna's birth
At midnight (nishita kaal), bathe Laddu Gopal with panchamrit and then water
Dress him in new clothes, adorn him with flute and peacock feather and place him in the cradle
Offer tulsi, makhan-mishri, panjiri and fruit
Rock the cradle, chant the mantras and sing Aarti Kunj Bihari Ki
Distribute prasad and break the fast as per custom
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Krishna).
The Mahamantra: a call to Krishna and Rama to engage us in devotion.

ganeshChaturthi.about: Ganesh Chaturthi, on the fourth day of the bright half of Bhadrapada, celebrates the birth of Lord Ganesha. Families bring home a clay idol, worship it for 1½, 3, 5, 7 or 10 days and then immerse it on Anant Chaturdashi.
ganeshChaturthi.story: Goddess Parvati created Ganesha from sandalwood paste and asked him to guard her door. When Shiva was stopped from entering, he cut off the boy's head; seeing Parvati's grief he restored Ganesha with an elephant's head and made him the first to be worshipped before any other god.
benefits: Removes obstacles from work, studies and family life
Brings wisdom, good beginnings and success
Unites families and communities in celebration
Ganesha is worshipped first for any new venture
dos: Bring an eco-friendly clay idol and install it at the madhyahna muhurat
Offer 21 durva blades, red flowers and modaks
Do aarti morning and evening while the idol is at home
Immerse the idol respectfully in water on the planned day
donts: Don't look at the Moon on Ganesh Chaturthi night; it is said to bring false blame (Mithya Dosh)
Don't offer tulsi to Ganesha
Avoid plaster-of-Paris idols that harm water bodies
Don't leave the idol alone at home
ganeshChaturthi.fasting: Optional. Many fast until the installation puja and then eat sattvic food.
samagri: Red cloth and a chowki (small stool)
Durva grass (21 blades) and red flowers, especially hibiscus
Kalash with water, mango leaves and coconut
Haldi, kumkum, chandan, akshat and janeu
steps: Clean the home and set a chowki with a red cloth
Place the kalash and then the Ganesha idol at the madhyahna muhurat
Invoke Ganesha (pranapratishtha) with flowers and akshat, chanting Om Gam Ganapataye Namah
Offer water, panchamrit, clothes, janeu, chandan and kumkum
Offer 21 durva blades, red flowers and modaks
Light the lamp and incense and sing Jai Ganesh Deva
Do aarti twice daily, and on the last day do uttar puja and immerse the idol
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Ganapati; 'Gam' is his seed sound.
O Lord with the curved trunk and mighty body, radiant as a million suns, please make all my work free of obstacles, always.

navratri.about: Sharad Navratri, from the first day of the bright half of Ashwin, is nine nights of worship of Goddess Durga in her nine forms: Shailputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta, Kushmanda, Skandamata, Katyayani, Kalaratri, Mahagauri and Siddhidatri. It ends with Dussehra on the tenth day.
navratri.story: The demon Mahishasura could not be defeated by any god. The combined energies of the gods became Goddess Durga, who fought him for nine days and killed him on the tenth. Navratri celebrates the triumph of divine feminine power over evil.
benefits: Brings the goddess's protection, strength and courage
Purifies body and mind through fasting and devotion
Each day's form blesses a different quality, from devotion to fulfilment
Kanya puja brings the goddess's blessing to the family
dos: Do ghatasthapana (kalash sthapana) in the morning of the first day
Keep an akhand jyoti (unbroken lamp) burning if you can
Worship that day's form of the goddess each day
Read the Durga Saptashati or Durga Chalisa
Do kanya puja on Ashtami or Navami
donts: Avoid onion, garlic, meat, alcohol and grains if fasting
Don't cut hair or nails during the nine days (traditional)
Don't let the akhand jyoti go out
Don't disrespect women or girls
navratri.fasting: Some fast all nine days on fruit, milk, kuttu, singhara and sabudana; others fast on the first and last days only.
samagri: Picture or idol of Goddess Durga
Kalash, mango leaves, coconut with red cloth
Clay pot with soil and barley (jau) for sowing
Kumkum, sindoor, haldi, akshat and red flowers
Fruit, sweets and items for kanya puja
steps: On day one, bathe and clean the altar
Sow barley in a clay pot of soil
Fill the kalash with water, place mango leaves and a coconut wrapped in red cloth, and set it beside the goddess (ghatasthapana)
Light the akhand jyoti
Each day worship that day's form with kumkum, red flowers, chunri and bhog
Read the Durga Saptashati or chant the mantras
Sing Jai Ambe Gauri in the morning and evening
On Ashtami or Navami worship nine young girls (kanya puja) and feed them
mantraMeanings: To the goddess who dwells in all beings as power, salutations again and again.
The Navarna mantra of Goddess Chamunda, for her protection and grace.

dussehra.about: Dussehra (Vijayadashami), on the tenth day of the bright half of Ashwin, celebrates the victory of good over evil: Lord Rama's victory over Ravana and Goddess Durga's over Mahishasura. Effigies of Ravana are burned in the evening.
dussehra.story: Ravana kidnapped Sita and refused to return her. After a long battle Rama killed Ravana on Vijayadashami and freed her. On the same day, after nine days of battle, Durga slew Mahishasura. The Pandavas also took back their weapons from the shami tree on this day after their exile.
benefits: Victory over enemies, fears and bad habits
Very auspicious for starting new ventures, learning or buying vehicles
Shami and Aparajita worship brings success
Celebrates truth and dharma in the family
dos: Worship Aparajita and the shami tree in the afternoon (vijay muhurat)
Clean and worship your tools, books and vehicles (shastra puja)
Exchange shami or apta leaves as 'gold' with friends
Watch Ravana Dahan and share sweets
donts: Avoid quarrels and harsh words
Avoid meat and alcohol
Don't start the day without remembering Rama
dussehra.fasting: No fast is needed. Navratri fasts are broken today.
samagri: Picture of Ram Darbar and Goddess Durga
Tools, books or vehicle for shastra puja
steps: Bathe and worship Ganesha first
Worship Ram Darbar and the goddess with roli, akshat and flowers
In the afternoon draw an eight-petalled lotus and worship Goddess Aparajita
Worship the shami tree and pray for victory
Clean your tools, books and vehicle, apply tilak and worship them
Sing the Ram stuti and aarti
Share shami leaves and sweets with family and friends
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Rama.
Salutations to Goddess Aparajita, the undefeated.

karvaChauth.deity: Goddess Parvati (Gauri), Lord Shiva and the Moon
karvaChauth.about: Karva Chauth, on the fourth day of the dark half of Kartika, is a fast kept by married women for their husbands' long life. They fast from sunrise without food or water, listen to the katha in the evening and break the fast after seeing the Moon.
karvaChauth.story: Queen Veeravati kept her first Karva Chauth at her parents' home. Seeing her faint with hunger, her brothers showed her a false Moon through a sieve and she broke her fast early; her husband then fell gravely ill. By keeping the fast faithfully for a year with Goddess Parvati's guidance, she won back his life.
benefits: Prayed for the husband's long life and good health
Strengthens love and trust between husband and wife
Brings the blessings of Shiva and Parvati for a happy marriage
Unmarried women may keep it for a good life partner
dos: Eat sargi (given by the mother-in-law) before sunrise
Dress up in solah shringar and wear red if you can
Listen to the Karva Chauth katha in the evening with other women
Offer arghya to the Moon, see it through a sieve and then your husband's face
Break the fast with water from your husband's hand
donts: Don't break the fast before moonrise
Don't use sharp objects (scissors, needles) or sleep in the day (traditional)
Don't wear black or white
Pregnant or unwell women should keep a lighter fast
karvaChauth.fasting: Nirjala from sunrise until the Moon is seen, after sargi before dawn. Those who can't may take water or fruit.
samagri: Karva (clay or metal pot) with water and a lid
Picture of Goddess Gauri, Shiva and family
Puja thali with a ghee diya
Bangles, bindi and other shringar items for the goddess
steps: Eat sargi before sunrise and take the sankalp to fast
In the evening dress up and prepare the puja thali
Place Goddess Gauri and the karva; draw the Karva Chauth picture if you use one
Offer roli, akshat, sindoor, flowers and shringar items to the goddess
Listen to the katha with other women, exchanging thalis seven times
When the Moon rises, offer arghya from the karva, then look at the Moon and your husband through the sieve
Take water and a sweet from your husband's hand to break the fast, and touch elders' feet
mantraMeanings: O Shivaa, Sharvani, beloved of Shiva, grant good fortune and fine children to the women devoted to you.
I bow to Shiva, the auspicious one.

dhanteras.deity: Lord Dhanvantari, Goddess Lakshmi, Kubera and Yama
dhanteras.about: Dhanteras (Dhantrayodashi), on the 13th day of the dark half of Kartika, begins the five days of Diwali. It honours Lord Dhanvantari, the physician of the gods, and invites wealth: people buy gold, silver or new utensils and light a lamp for Yama in the evening.
dhanteras.story: During the churning of the ocean Lord Dhanvantari rose carrying the pot of amrit, so this is also National Ayurveda Day. In another story, King Hima's son was destined to die of a snakebite on the fourth night of his marriage; his wife lit lamps and piled gold at the door, and Yama, dazzled, left. Hence the Yama deepdaan.
benefits: Brings good health through Dhanvantari's blessing
Invites wealth and prosperity for the year
The Yama deepdaan is believed to protect the family from untimely death
Buying new metal items today is considered very auspicious
dos: Clean the home and decorate the entrance
Buy a new utensil, gold, silver or a broom
Worship Dhanvantari, Lakshmi and Kubera in the pradosh kaal
Light a four-wicked lamp facing south outside the home for Yama
donts: Don't buy iron, sharp objects or black items today (traditional)
Don't lend money today
Don't leave the home dark in the evening
dhanteras.fasting: No fast is needed; some fast until the evening puja.
samagri: Pictures of Dhanvantari, Lakshmi and Kubera
New utensil, coin or jewellery bought today
Ghee lamps and a four-faced clay diya for Yama
steps: Clean the home and draw rangoli at the door
In the pradosh kaal, set the deities on a chowki with red cloth
Worship Ganesha first, then Dhanvantari, Lakshmi and Kubera with roli, akshat and flowers
Place the new item you bought before them and worship it
Offer sweets, dhaniya and jaggery and sing the Lakshmi aarti
Light a four-faced lamp outside, facing south, for Yama with the deepdaan mantra
Light lamps across the home
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Dhanvantari, the divine physician.
By this lamp offered on Trayodashi, may Yama, son of the Sun, with his noose and staff, Kala and Shyama, be pleased with me.

diwali.about: Diwali, the festival of lights, falls on the new moon (Amavasya) of Kartika. Homes are lit with diyas, and Lakshmi Puja is done in the evening pradosh kaal, ideally in the sthir lagna, to invite wealth, prosperity and happiness.
diwali.story: Lord Rama returned to Ayodhya on this night after defeating Ravana, and the people lit rows of lamps to welcome him. It is also the night Goddess Lakshmi appeared from the churning of the ocean and chose Vishnu as her husband. In Bengal, Kali Puja is celebrated on the same night.
benefits: Invites Lakshmi's blessings of wealth and abundance
Ganesha's worship removes obstacles for the year
Lights drive away darkness, negativity and poverty
A new beginning for business: many start new account books (chopda puja)
dos: Clean and decorate the whole home before evening
Do Lakshmi-Ganesh puja in the pradosh kaal, ideally in sthir lagna
Light diyas in every room, at the door and on the terrace
Keep the main door open during puja to welcome Lakshmi
Share sweets and gifts and give to the needy
donts: Don't leave any corner of the home dark or dirty
Don't sleep or quarrel during the puja time
Avoid gambling and alcohol
Don't burn loud or polluting crackers near animals and the elderly
diwali.fasting: Optional. Some fast until the evening Lakshmi Puja and then share the festive meal.
samagri: New idols or pictures of Lakshmi and Ganesha
Kalash with water, mango leaves and coconut
Lotus or red flowers and marigold
Roli, akshat, chandan, haldi and kumkum
Many diyas, ghee, incense and camphor
steps: Clean the home, draw rangoli and put up a toran
In the pradosh kaal set Lakshmi and Ganesha on a red cloth, Ganesha on Lakshmi's left
Set up the kalash and invoke the deities with flowers and akshat
Worship Ganesha first with durva and modak, then Lakshmi with lotus, kumkum and coins
Offer kheel-batashe, sweets and fruit and worship account books and jewellery
Chant the mantras and sing Jai Ganesh Deva and Om Jai Lakshmi Mata
Light diyas throughout the home and keep one lamp burning all night
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Ganapati; 'Gam' is his seed sound.
O Lakshmi who dwells in the lotus, be pleased with me; salutations to Mahalakshmi.

devUthaniEkadashi.about: Dev Uthani (Prabodhini) Ekadashi, on the 11th day of the bright half of Kartika, is when Lord Vishnu awakens from his four-month rest. Chaturmas ends, the wedding season begins, and Tulsi Vivah (the marriage of Tulsi with Shaligram) is celebrated.
devUthaniEkadashi.story: Vrinda, the devoted wife of Jalandhar, became the tulsi plant, and Vishnu promised to marry her as Shaligram. On Dev Uthani Ekadashi families celebrate Tulsi Vivah, marrying the tulsi plant to Shaligram or Krishna with full wedding rites.
benefits: Ends Chaturmas, so weddings and griha pravesh can resume
Tulsi Vivah is said to give the merit of a kanyadaan
Awakens Vishnu's blessings for the household
Removes sins and brings peace
dos: Wake early, bathe and take a sankalp for the fast
Chant Vishnu's name or read the Vishnu Sahasranama
Offer tulsi leaves to Lord Vishnu
Stay awake longer in the evening for bhajan if you can
Break the fast (parana) the next morning within the Dwadashi time
Wake Lord Vishnu with conch, bells and the awakening mantra
Celebrate Tulsi Vivah: dress the tulsi as a bride and marry her to Shaligram
donts: Don't eat rice or grains, even if you are not fasting
Don't pluck tulsi leaves on Ekadashi; pick them the day before
Avoid onion, garlic, alcohol and meat
Avoid anger, gossip and sleeping in the day
devUthaniEkadashi.fasting: Phalahar or nirjala as your health allows; parana next morning in the Dwadashi time.
samagri: Picture or idol of Lord Vishnu or Krishna
Fruits, dry fruits and sweets for bhog
Tulsi plant in a pot, red chunri and shringar items for Tulsi Vivah
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp for the fast
Draw Vishnu's footprints with rice paste at the altar
Worship Vishnu with panchamrit, tulsi and yellow flowers
In the evening wake him with conch and bells, chanting Uttishtha Govinda
Build a small mandap of sugarcane around the tulsi plant
Dress the tulsi in a red chunri and marry her to Shaligram with mantras and pheras
Sing the aarti, share prasad and break the fast next morning
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu).
Rise, O Govinda, Lord of the world, leave your sleep; while you sleep the whole world sleeps.

ekadashi.about: Ekadashi, the 11th day of each lunar fortnight, comes twice a month and is the most observed vrat for Lord Vishnu. Fasting from grains and spending the day in devotion is believed to purify body and mind.
ekadashi.story: The Padma Purana says a goddess named Ekadashi was born from Vishnu's body and defeated the demon Mura while Vishnu slept. Pleased, Vishnu blessed her: whoever fasts on her day will be freed of sins. Each of the 24 Ekadashis has its own name and katha.
benefits: Purifies body and mind; fasting gives the digestion rest
Brings Vishnu's grace and inner peace
Builds self-discipline and devotion
Said to remove sins and lead to liberation
dos: Wake early, bathe and take a sankalp for the fast
Chant Vishnu's name or read the Vishnu Sahasranama
Offer tulsi leaves to Lord Vishnu
Stay awake longer in the evening for bhajan if you can
Break the fast (parana) the next morning within the Dwadashi time
donts: Don't eat rice or grains, even if you are not fasting
Don't pluck tulsi leaves on Ekadashi; pick them the day before
Avoid onion, garlic, alcohol and meat
Avoid anger, gossip and sleeping in the day
ekadashi.fasting: Avoid grains and beans. Choose nirjala, fruit and milk, or one meal of sabudana, kuttu, singhara and potatoes. Parana next morning in the Dwadashi time.
samagri: Picture or idol of Lord Vishnu or Krishna
Fruits, dry fruits and sweets for bhog
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp for the fast
Place Lord Vishnu or Krishna on a yellow cloth
Offer panchamrit, chandan, yellow flowers and tulsi
Light the lamp and chant Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya 108 times
Read that Ekadashi's katha
Sing Om Jai Jagdish Hare
Break the fast next morning after puja, in the Dwadashi time
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu), the indweller of all.

purnima.about: Purnima, the full moon, is an auspicious day each month for fasting, charity and Satyanarayan katha. Devotees take a holy dip, worship Vishnu and offer water to the full Moon in the evening.
purnima.story: In the Satyanarayan katha, Lord Vishnu tells sage Narada that anyone who worships him as Satyanarayan with faith will be freed of troubles. The stories of a poor Brahmin, a woodcutter and a merchant show how keeping the vow brought prosperity, and forgetting it brought trouble.
benefits: Brings peace of mind; the full Moon strengthens the mind
Satyanarayan puja brings prosperity and fulfils wishes
Charity today is especially meritorious
Good for meditation and spiritual practice
dos: Take a bath, in a holy river if possible
Do Satyanarayan puja and read the katha
Offer arghya (water with milk) to the Moon after moonrise
Donate food, clothes or money
donts: Avoid meat and alcohol
Avoid anger and arguments; the mind is said to be more sensitive today
Don't skip the prasad after the katha
purnima.fasting: Optional. Many fast until the evening puja and Moon arghya, eating fruit and milk.
samagri: Banana leaves or stems for the mandap
Prasad: sheera (suji halwa) with banana, or panjiri
Lota with water and milk for the Moon
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp
Set up the altar with banana leaves and the Satyanarayan picture
Worship Ganesha first, then Satyanarayan with panchamrit, tulsi, chandan and flowers
Read the five chapters of the Satyanarayan katha
Offer the prasad and sing Om Jai Jagdish Hare
After moonrise offer water with milk to the Moon
Distribute prasad to everyone present
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva (Vishnu).
Salutations to Soma, the Moon.

amavasya.about: Amavasya, the new moon, is the day dedicated to ancestors. People offer tarpan, give charity and pray for the peace of departed family members. It is a quiet day for reflection rather than celebration.
amavasya.story: Tradition says the ancestors come to receive offerings on Amavasya, especially during Pitru Paksha. In the Mahabharata, Karna received only gold in the afterlife because he had never offered food to his ancestors; he was allowed back to earth for fifteen days to make the offerings, which is the root of Pitru Paksha.
benefits: Brings the blessings of ancestors and peace to the family
Said to ease Pitru dosh and family troubles
Charity and feeding others bring great merit
Good for introspection and meditation
dos: Offer tarpan (water with black sesame) to ancestors at midday
Feed cows, crows, dogs and the needy
Light a mustard-oil lamp under a peepal tree in the evening
Remember your ancestors and pray for them
donts: Avoid starting new work, buying a home or holding celebrations
Avoid meat, alcohol, onion and garlic
Don't cut hair or nails (traditional)
Avoid lonely places at night (traditional)
amavasya.fasting: Optional. Some keep a fast or eat one sattvic meal after the tarpan.
samagri: Food for cows, crows and dogs
Mustard oil and a diya for the peepal tree
steps: Bathe and wear clean clothes
At midday, face south, holding kusha grass
Offer water mixed with black sesame to your ancestors, saying their names if you know them
Offer food to cows, crows and dogs
Give food or clothes to someone in need
In the evening light a mustard-oil lamp under a peepal tree
Chant Om Namah Shivaya and pray for the family's peace
mantraMeanings: Salutations to the ancestors.
I bow to Shiva, the auspicious one.

pradosh.about: Pradosh Vrat falls on the 13th day (Trayodashi) of each lunar fortnight, twice a month. Shiva is worshipped at twilight in the pradosh kaal, when he is said to dance in joy on Mount Kailash. It is called Som Pradosh on a Monday and Shani Pradosh on a Saturday.
pradosh.story: When the ocean was churned, deadly halahal poison rose first. Shiva drank it to save the world, and Parvati stopped it in his throat, turning it blue. It is said the gods worshipped him at twilight on Trayodashi in gratitude, and he danced between his bull Nandi's horns.
benefits: Removes sins and brings Shiva's protection
Each weekday's Pradosh gives its own blessing, from health to children
Brings peace, prosperity and harmony
Good for clearing the effects of Saturn on Shani Pradosh
dos: Fast through the day
Bathe again before sunset and wear clean clothes
Worship Shiva in the pradosh kaal with abhishek and bel leaves
Read the Pradosh katha and chant Om Namah Shivaya
donts: Don't offer tulsi, ketaki or turmeric to Shiva
Avoid grains, onion, garlic and alcohol during the fast
Don't sleep in the day
pradosh.fasting: Fruit and milk through the day; a sattvic meal after the evening puja.
samagri: Shivling or a picture of Lord Shiva
Water and raw milk for abhishek
Bel (bilva) leaves, ideally with three leaflets
Dhatura, aak flowers and white flowers
Akshat (whole rice), honey, curd, ghee and sugar
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp
Bathe again before sunset and sit facing north-east
In the pradosh kaal, worship Ganesha, then Shiva and Parvati
Bathe the Shivling with water, milk and Ganga jal
Offer chandan, bel leaves, dhatura and white flowers
Read the Pradosh vrat katha and chant Om Namah Shivaya 108 times
Sing the Shiv aarti and break the fast with a sattvic meal
mantraMeanings: I bow to Shiva, the auspicious one.
We worship the three-eyed Lord who nourishes all; may he free us from death as a ripe cucumber falls from its vine, and grant immortality.

sankashti.about: Sankashti Chaturthi falls on the fourth day of the dark half of every lunar month. 'Sankashti' means deliverance from trouble: devotees fast all day and break the fast after worshipping Ganesha and seeing the Moon. When it falls on a Tuesday it is Angaraki Chaturthi, considered especially powerful.
sankashti.story: Once, when the gods were in trouble, Shiva asked Ganesha and Kartikeya who could remove it. To win a race around the world, Ganesha simply circled his parents, saying they were his world. Pleased, Shiva blessed him as the remover of troubles and said those who worship him on Chaturthi will be freed of difficulties.
benefits: Removes troubles, debts and obstacles
Blesses children with health and studies
Angaraki Sankashti is said to give the merit of a year's Sankashtis
Brings peace and success to the family
dos: Fast through the day
Worship Ganesha in the evening with durva and modaks
See the Moon after moonrise and offer arghya
Read the Sankashti katha and then break the fast
donts: Don't break the fast before the Moon is seen
Don't offer tulsi to Ganesha
Avoid grains, onion and garlic during the fast
sankashti.fasting: Fruit, milk and sabudana through the day; the fast is broken after seeing the Moon.
samagri: Lota with water, milk and akshat for the Moon
steps: Bathe and take the sankalp in the morning
In the evening set up Ganesha on a red cloth
Offer roli, akshat, durva, red flowers and modak
Light the lamp, chant Om Gam Ganapataye Namah and read the Sankashti katha
Sing Jai Ganesh Deva
After moonrise offer water with milk and akshat to the Moon
Break the fast with prasad
mantraMeanings: Salutations to Lord Ganapati; 'Gam' is his seed sound.
O Lord with the curved trunk and mighty body, radiant as a million suns, please make all my work free of obstacles, always.

masikShivaratri.about: Masik Shivaratri falls on the 14th night of the dark half of every lunar month. It is a monthly night of Shiva worship; the one in Phalguna is Maha Shivaratri. Devotees fast and worship Shiva, especially around midnight (nishita kaal).
masikShivaratri.story: It is said that Goddess Lakshmi, Saraswati, Indrani, Gayatri, Savitri, Sita, Parvati and Rati all kept the Masik Shivaratri vrat and won Shiva's grace. Keeping it every month is believed to make even difficult wishes come true.
benefits: Brings Shiva's grace and peace of mind
Said to help with marriage and harmony in married life
Helps control anger, desire and other inner obstacles
Monthly practice builds steady devotion
dos: Fast through the day
Worship Shiva at night, ideally in the nishita kaal
Offer water, milk and bel leaves to the Shivling
Chant Om Namah Shivaya or the Mahamrityunjaya mantra
donts: Don't offer tulsi, ketaki or turmeric to Shiva
Avoid grains, onion, garlic and alcohol
Don't sleep during the night puja
masikShivaratri.fasting: Fruit and milk through the day; break the fast the next morning after puja.
samagri: Shivling or a picture of Lord Shiva
Water and raw milk for abhishek
Bel (bilva) leaves, ideally with three leaflets
Dhatura, aak flowers and white flowers
Akshat (whole rice), honey, curd, ghee and sugar
steps: Bathe early and take the sankalp
In the evening bathe again and prepare the altar
At night bathe the Shivling with water and milk, chanting Om Namah Shivaya
Offer chandan, bel leaves, dhatura and white flowers
Light the lamp and chant the Mahamrityunjaya mantra 108 times
Sing the Shiv aarti
Next morning do a short puja and break the fast
mantraMeanings: I bow to Shiva, the auspicious one.
We worship the three-eyed Lord who nourishes all; may he free us from death as a ripe cucumber falls from its vine, and grant immortality.
